keyVerseText: And turneth toward the sunrising to Bethdagon, and reacheth to Zebulun, and to the valley of Jiphthahel toward the north side of Bethemek, and Neiel, and goeth out to Cabul on the left hand,
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun כָּבוּל (Kâbûwl) derives from the same root as כֶּבֶל (kebel), meaning fetter or bond, conveying a sense of limitation or binding. This etymology suggests that the name carries a connotation of restriction or sterility, which contrasts with its use as a place name. Understanding this root enriches the meaning beyond a mere geographic label, hinting at a place characterized metaphorically by constraint or barrenness.
usageInScripture: The word כָּבוּל appears twice in Scripture, both times as a proper name referring to locations in Palestine: once as a city on the border of Asher (Joshua 19:27) and once as a district in Galilee given by Solomon to Hiram (1 Kings 9:13). Its translations consistently reflect this geographic identity, either 'to Cabul' or 'of Cabul,' emphasizing its function as a place name rather than a common noun. This consistent usage underscores its importance as a defined territorial marker within Israel's tribal and administrative boundaries.
theologicalSignificance: Theologically, the name כָּבוּל, rooted in the concept of binding or limitation, invites reflection on God's sovereign boundaries and the order He establishes in creation and covenant. The fact that one district named Cabul was given by Solomon to Hiram yet was contemptuously regarded suggests human perspectives on divine provision and stewardship can vary. For believers, recognizing that even places with names implying limitation fall under God's sovereign plan reminds us that God’s purposes transcend human judgment and that He can redeem all circumstances for His glory. This calls the Christian to trust in God's providential governance over all lands and peoples.
keyVerseReflection: Joshua 19:27 mentions Cabul as a boundary marker, stating the territory 'goeth out to Cabul on the left hand.' The use of the name here grounds the tribal allotment in a tangible geographic reality, emphasizing the precision and order in God's distribution of the Promised Land. The word Cabul, with its root meaning of binding, subtly underscores the idea of divinely set limits and boundaries that shape the inheritance of God's people, reminding believers of the faithfulness and exactness of God's promises.
